summary: One blocking finding, STU-013, and it is repaired; it is against the leaf's tracked audit record and not against any reader-facing prose. The author-study \AIModelContribution declaration in generation-metadata.tex closed its iteration-5 clause by reporting two standing advisories cleared, the second of them 'the third reading's use of Aquinas on Dan 9:18 recorded in the interpretation audit, whose witnesses, element table and moral sense now agree with the manifest and the section'. Each of those three assertions was checked here and each is false: research/interpretations.md names Thomas Aquinas nowhere in section 3 -- not in the 3.2 witnesses, not in the 3.3 Offertory row (still 'Jerome on 9:5-23; Augustine De pecc. mer. II sect. 13; Rupert, Durandus (chant)'), not in the 3.4 moral sense, and not in that lane's row of 'The three readings in brief' (still 'Augustine; Jerome; Cassiodorus; Hilary; Robert Bellarmine; with Rupert and Durandus for the chants'); the file's header note records revisions through the fourth research reentry and none at iteration 5; and the file is byte-identical to its last committed state, so it agrees neither with proper-components.toml, which declares Aquinas for that lane, nor with sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex, which develops him there. The clause now reports what iteration 5 actually did: the STU-011 psalm-locus repair, the one advisory it cleared (STU-012, the second reading's closing remark on the Postcommunion), and the other advisory left uncleared and reported to its owner, with the reason -- research/interpretations.md is the research stage's file and repairing it from author-study would be the silent revision of a reviewed upstream document the contract forbids. That is now in agreement with the 'STU-006, advisory, not cleared, and why' entry of research/production-review.md, which the record previously contradicted. The study stage corrected the record and did not make the claim true: research/interpretations.md is byte-identical to how this dispatch found it, and no record of the leaf now states that the Aquinas repair has been done. Both of this round's standing advisories against study-owned prose are cleared while in those files. STU-014: Ps 109 was the one psalm the study cited that never carried its modern number, against the convention the head of sections/05-appointed-texts.tex states and the 1962 profile requires; the note after the Gospel now reads 'Ps 109:1 (Heb. 110:1) in verse 44', the conversion read in the repository's own tracked concordance, artifact psalm-numbering-ee3c7757 of the Douay-Rheims Challoner edition the study quotes, whose row for Vulgate Ps 109 gives Hebrew and English Ps 110 at an offset of none, uniform through the psalm. Later bare uses stand as the other psalms' later bare uses do, and every psalm the study cites -- Pss 13, 32, 52, 75, 101, 109 and 118 -- now carries its Hebrew number at first use. STU-015: the second reading's Postcommunion paragraph ended 'which RG 115~a completes', the only occurrence of that abbreviation in the reader-facing argument and one the body nowhere expands; it now reads 'which the general rubrics complete (no. 115 a)', the form sections/05-appointed-texts.tex already uses at the Secret, so the same rubric is cited one way throughout the body. The fact is unchanged: propers/verified.md section 8 records that the typical edition prints the conclusion only as far as in unitate and that Rubricae generales n. 115 a, read on the page image at printed p. XIX, gives the full form. The abbreviation survives only in the terminal appendix, where the References on the following page expand it, which is what the advisory allowed. STU-006 is not reported here and was not touched: it needs its research owner. The settled proof is build/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf, SHA-256 9953a1fb142c938c160cf6b59fbc35430e12fc5e2f1120e0a05f27526bb061ad, 38 physical pages (inside 20-50), letter, Palatino at 11/15, revision timestamp 2026-09-19T05:45:00Z, which the PDF's own ModDate carries. It settles in two passes, and two independent builds from a removed PDF, log and auxiliary file produced identical bytes, so the proof is a cold fixed point; the log has no error, no LaTeX Warning, no package warning (the fancyhdr headheight warning a wrapped head would raise is absent), no overfull or underfull box, no undefined reference and no rerun request. The extent and the pagination are unchanged: the contents file and the auxiliary file are byte-identical to those of iterations 4 and 5 (4274428cbe0909d605fbb4b80de5f17d1ab066e01df1a6e0a85afb6b59ce3c3c and 424bc0ef72e2d0ac85f563b68d162d8215fd8194b71d44336471adebd423eeb9), so no heading, float or cross-reference moved and the page numbers the study review cites still name the passages it read. Four pages differ in extracted text and only four: page 6 and page 24 carry the two repaired clauses, page 38 the new timestamp, and page 25 receives one line -- the STU-015 clause is three words longer than what it replaced and lengthens its paragraph by one line, so 'such Sunday. What remains firm is the Gospel's second half ...' now opens page 25 instead of closing page 24. That is a reflow within one paragraph across a break already there, not a repagination; the heading 'The four senses of this reading' and everything after it stand where they stood, and both pages were inspected. Extent: 19,247 words by the same pdftotext -layout measure the iteration-5 record used against that proof's 19,242, and a multiset diff of the two extractions accounts for all five with nothing over -- two tokens added by '(Heb. 110:1)', three by turning 'RG 115 a completes.' into 'the general rubrics complete (no. 115 a).', and the timestamp one token exchanged for another. Measured as substantive words instead -- the six argumentative components through Pandoc's LaTeX AST with headings and tables removed -- this iteration's implementation counts 12,767 before and 12,770 now, a gain of 3, all in sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex; the STU-014 repair falls in sections/05-appointed-texts.tex, which that measure excludes. As at iterations 2, 4 and 5 the absolute figure does not reproduce the record's earlier ones, so only the delta is comparable. All seventeen checks pass at these bytes, with their invocations and output kept beside the proof: check-proper-components (artifacts/research), scripts/_proper_study.py check (content/research, --require-presentation), all twelve check-content-preflight checks the study gate names including provenance-matches-run against this packet's header, check-generation-metadata, check-web-edition, and a trial tools/web-edition conversion, which carries both repaired clauses through intact. A leaf-edition preflight sweep also passes. All 38 pages were rendered and both contact sheets read, with pages 6, 24, 25 and 38 inspected individually: no blank page, no heading-only page, no clipping, collision or missing text, every running head a single line. Both companions were rebuilt against the changed shared generation-metadata.tex and build cleanly at their unchanged extents, 12 and 5 pages; they are the derivation stages' to rewrite. Files touched: generation-metadata.tex (timestamp and the author-study contribution), sections/05-appointed-texts.tex, sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex and research/production-review.md, which records the repair, the two cleared advisories, the one standing against the research owner, the word counts and the proof. No research evidence was changed and no claim was weakened to make anything pass. The shared-timestamp three-document build and the independent reviews remain the workflow's to obtain.
